proof:
The projection of the lifted hull is $[0,2]$ and its endpoint fibers are the displayed ones. At base one a convex representation has equal weights at the endpoint bases. Their midpoint rectangle has coordinate bounds $1/100$ and $101/200$, so its maximum $K_1$ gauge is $1/100+(5/3)(101/200)=511/600<1$. Thus every representation at base one remains in $K_1$. It is exactly that fiber because the hull includes it; the hull is full-dimensional because the middle layer has area and the base projection has length. All three fibers contain $0$ in their interiors.

The strict-side pushforward from accepted fact f35472644bdd7a6c at $(0,0)$ is $f=\mathbf1_{K_1}+4\mathbf1_{K_2/2}$, with $0$ in both projected sets. For a nonzero vector $v$, the integral $I(v)=2\int_0^\infty t f(tv)\,dt$ is the sum of the squared parameters $\max\{t\ge0:tv\in K_i\}$ for $i=1,2$, as the coefficient $4$ cancels the squared factor $1/2$ in the second radial bound. The gauge of $B$ is $I(v)^{-1/2}$ by radial rescaling. The points $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ are in $B$ because they are in $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively, so their convex combination $p=(1/10,9/10)$ lies in $\operatorname{conv}(B)$. Its ray parameter in $K_1$ is $1/(1/10+(5/3)(9/10))=5/8$. In $K_2$ it is $\min(1/10,10/9)=1/10$. Thus $I(p)=(5/8)^2+(1/10)^2=641/1600<1/2$, whereas membership in $\sqrt2B$ would require $2I(p)\ge1$.

statement:
There is a planar strict-midpoint-compatible example with $\operatorname{conv}(B)\nsubseteq\sqrt2B$ for the positive-side slope Ball body about $(0,0)$. Use the actual integer fibers
$$
K_0=[-1/100,1/100]^2,\qquad K_1=\{(x,y):|x|+(5/3)|y|\le1\},\qquad
K_2=[-1/100,1/100]\times[-1,1]
$$
of their lifted hull at bases $0,1,2$. The midpoint body $(K_0+K_2)/2$ lies in the interior of $K_1$. For $f=\mathbf1_{K_1}+4\mathbf1_{K_2/2}$ use $\rho_B(e)^2=2\int_0^\infty t f(te)\,dt$ in unit directions. The point $p=(1/10,9/10)\in\operatorname{conv}(B)$ satisfies $2\int_0^\infty t f(tp)\,dt=641/1600<1/2$.
title: Sampled Ball dilation fails with strict midpoint compatibility
